pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts the existing rows are all 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test stars item 2 and expects exactly ['First item','★ Second item','Third item']. The ★ comes from item() in src/index.js.
The 'AC-3' test stars items 3 and 1 and expects only those two, in id order, with status 200. The query is WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id.
The 'AC-4' test checks both / and /?show=all and expects all three items in id order with the star on item 3.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact anchors: 'Starred only' on the full list and 'All items' on the starred list.
The 'AC-6' test requests Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__. Each answers 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.

traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. The 'AC-7' test asserts this. The traffic Worker builds the request URL from the path string, so the query is preserved. The route checker was updated to accept it.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the route-checker tweak that AC-7 needs.
All 7 acceptance items are named by tests. All four rows of the state table have a test. The spec was added in the same change as the code, with the go dated 2026-10-12, and no later commit edits it.

The tests assert rendered output and status codes, and would fail on wrong code. The traffic fake app and the route-checker script tests were extended, not loosened. I did not run the tests here; CI covers that.
The README describes the ?show=starred view. Nothing stale.
Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup. The SQL is built only from fixed view strings. Titles are escaped. A repeated show parameter uses the first value.
The query value is never interpolated. Only the fixed VIEWS entries reach the SQL. The 400 body is a static string.
The diff changes the Worker's HTML output only and adds no UI or style files, so there is no designed interface to review.
There are no UI files or browser flows. The HTML is checked by Worker-level tests.
The claims match the diff: behaviour, the route-checker change, the fake-app change, the migration, the README and the routes file. The title is under 72 characters.
